PullRequest.Title: agentHost: migrate to Microsoft Copilot SDK v2
PullRequest.Body:

Migrate Agent Host from `@github/copilot-sdk@1.0.33-preview.0` / runtime `1.0.111-0` to `@microsoft/copilot-sdk@2.0.0-preview.2` / runtime `1.0.113-1`.

Latest conflict resolution: `d3f13f2698e3aad26940115bd40186f5a9879831` merges main through `c0b608a6e82bf47e202987c918913fd4a6deb748`. It preserves upstream Canvas extension-data sandbox grants through SDK v2's grouped extension and permission options, with create/resume regressions for enabled and disabled extensions. The preceding merge also preserves upstream subagent chat links, the shared Connector fixture, and MCP diagnostics while retaining spawned SDK v2 clients. No SDK/runtime versions, permission assertions, or generated baselines changed. The older revision-specific results below remain historical. (Written by Copilot)

V2 defaults to hosting the native runtime in-process. VS Code deliberately retains a separate runtime process using `runtime: RuntimeConnection.forSpawnedStdio(...)`, including scoped clients, certificate commands, and direct SDK tests. Storage-only clients remain in `empty` mode; ordinary coding clients explicitly select the renamed `coding-agent` mode.

Local tests, GitHub CI, and both Azure SDK Validation builds passed for `59323a1838e7e7ab34b4f08294c6b1ab74db01a2`. The subsequent conflict-resolution merge is `0fcfcdff1cd4d7313bf7deef1c81e7c6e415a066`; its client type-check, lint/hygiene, 3,358 owning unit tests (1 existing pending), and 2 native account/restart integration tests passed. GitHub CI for that new revision is pending; the earlier full GitHub/Azure results below are historical, not final-SHA results for the merge. **Validation gap: the four full-app Linux DEB/RPM dependency-reference checks were not run.** The SDK-only native dependency comparisons passed, but they are not a substitute for the full-app check.

The follow-up merge preserves main's missing-plugin-directory filtering in v2's `plugins.directories`, reopened Microsoft session sign-in, and read-only legacy history recovery. The newly added recovery helper uses the renamed SDK types and retains validated v1 `parentToolCallId` fields for old saved journals without treating them as current live-event fields. No SDK/runtime versions, permission assertions, or generated baselines changed during conflict resolution.

## Change ledger

| Files/surface | Exact change | Why necessary | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root/remote `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (6 files) | Rename the SDK and its eight optional platform packages, pin SDK `2.0.0-preview.2` and runtime `1.0.113-1`, and extend the existing Copilot release-age exception to the renamed SDK family. Both locks retain SHA-512 pins without explicit SDK tarball URLs. | Desktop and remote must bundle the same release; the existing package-age exception must follow the package rename. | Expected upgrade; unrelated dependency resolutions are preserved. |
| `build/.moduleignore`, `build/darwin/create-universal-app.ts`, `build/lib/copilot.ts`, `build/lib/test/copilot.test.ts` (4 files) | Resolve/cross-copy SDK assets under `@microsoft`, retain the selected architecture's runtime, preserve optional-payload exclusions and standalone-CLI exclusions, and keep Koffi excluded because the runtime remains out-of-process. | Renaming imports alone would omit the shipped runtime or break cross-architecture packaging. | Expected packaging adaptation. |
| `cglicenses.json` | Rename the SDK license override and point it to the new public Microsoft SDK repository's MIT license. | The npm archive still omits the license file. | Expected attribution adaptation. |
| `copilotAccountService.ts`, `copilotAgent.ts`, `copilotAgentSession.ts`, `copilotGitHubCredentials.ts`, `copilotMcpSkillConsent.ts`, `copilotPromptAttribution.ts`, `copilotRuntimePaths.ts`, `copilotSandboxCertificateCli.ts`, `copilotSessionLauncher.ts`, `copilotSessionWrapper.ts`, `mapSessionEvents.ts` (11 files under `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot`) | Migrate client/session options and mutable RPC payloads into v2's groups; preserve nested siblings on create/resume/retry; retain credential exclusivity, policy injection, sandbox settings, tool filters, telemetry and callbacks. Use `agentId` for live subagent attribution and append-only `tool.shell_output` events instead of the removed cumulative event. Read legacy transcript attribution through the existing guarded property reader. | V2 removes the old flat API and deprecated live events; saved v1 transcripts still need to restore correctly. | Expected compatibility adaptation; no permission or approval assertions removed. |
| 29 SDK-owning unit/direct-provider/E2E test and helper files under `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node` | Update typed mocks, option projections, embedded extension programs, mandatory modes, canonical billing fields and explicit named BYOK routing. Assert spawned-stdio options at the test boundary. Migrate shell-output cases to sequenced chunks while retaining output, artifact, cleanup and duplicate-chunk assertions; migrate live child-usage cases to envelope attribution. | Tests must exercise the real v2 API rather than silently pass retired option names through JavaScript or partial mocks. | Expected test adaptations; existing credential/platform gates remain. |
| One generated snapshot: `test/node/__snapshots__/Copilot_SDK_-_managed_settings_bundled_managedSettings_schema_matches_the_snapshot.schema.json` | Add `features.browserUse` and its deny-wins description; update the feature-map description to cover the new native MDM leaf. Generated with the supported tokenless update flag, then tested strictly. | Runtime-owned managed-settings schema expansion. | Reviewed expected schema addition; no broad baseline refresh. |
| `src/vs/platform/agentHost/AGENTS.md`, `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotBuiltinSkills.ts` (2 files) | Document the new SDK identity/types and teach Agent Host troubleshooting to join envelope `agentId` to `subagent.started.data.toolCallId`, retaining the deprecated field only for old logs. | Agent Host-owned guidance must describe the API and event attribution it actually runs. | Expected documentation adaptation. The standalone CLI's create-canvas skill and its test are unchanged: that CLI bundles its own v1 SDK and its authoring skill does not target Agent Host sessions. Existing user-authored v1 Agent Host extensions may need import/options migration. |
| `src/vs/platform/dialogs/test/electron-browser/dialog.test.ts` | Select both the standalone CLI and renamed SDK About-dialog lines explicitly. | CI found that the old shared test selector discarded the correctly renamed SDK line before comparing version-formatting results. | Expected test adaptation; all 12 owning cases pass, and the final GitHub workflow passes. |
| 104 remaining files (listed below) | Exact `@github/copilot-sdk` to `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` reference replacements only: imports/types, SDK paths, packaging/signing filters, canary configuration, documentation, and associated tests. | All consumers must resolve the renamed package, including platform packaging and canary tooling. The standalone `@github/copilot` CLI name is unchanged. | Mechanical identity migration only. |

The full 24-case model prompt matrix passes **without prompt baseline changes**. No model-set or tool-inventory snapshot was regenerated. The separately maintained upgrade skill and portable-lock helper were also migrated locally; their helper tests pass, but those user-level files are not part of this repository diff.

## Acceptance status

The detailed acceptance snapshot below applies to revision `59323a1838e7e7ab34b4f08294c6b1ab74db01a2`, which merged main through `fc08017c2e82db30a3196c86bcdb46a283e18b37`. Affected types, owning unit suites, focused integrations, the complete deterministic runner, and supplemental acceptance were rerun after that merge. The documentation ownership correction was checked with the owning Agent Host and standalone CLI skill suites. The follow-up merge through `06bea887795fc42064969eb06b524ad0d02f2781` and its newer focused validation are described above. Local results below are macOS arm64 unless stated otherwise; counts from overlapping selections are not additive.

The pre-follow-up merge-base inventory accounts for **159 files: 104 exact package-reference-only replacements and 55 substantive/configuration/test/documentation files** in the ledger above. The conflict-resolution merge additionally adapts the new upstream `copilotSessionHistoryRecovery.ts` helper as described above. Upstream changes brought in by either merge are not themselves SDK changes.

- Root/remote frozen install and portable nine-package SDK resolution verification passed. Canonical npm was unreachable locally; lock generation used the configured mirror, preserving integrity verification and removing only SDK mirror URL overrides.
- Client and build-tool type checks, layer checks, packaging/canary/universal-app helper tests (36), and commit hygiene passed.
- All direct `copilotSdk*` integration entrypoints: **38 passed** in the standalone batch. Initial discovery had four canvas failures caused by embedded extensions still using flat v1 options, plus the expected managed-schema difference; the complete strict batch subsequently passed. After the main merge, the combined SDK/prompt/native-account selection passed **62 tests**. The explicit native-account restart selection also passed **2 tests**, including the actual restart scenario.
- Full Copilot prompt matrix: **24 passed**, no baseline changes; included again in the post-merge combined selection.
- SDK-owning lifecycle/adaptation unit batch: **3,372 passed, 1 existing pending** before the merge. The first run exposed obsolete typed mock/expected option shapes; the complete batch passed after migration. The affected post-merge lifecycle/account/worktree selection passed **3,253 tests, 1 existing pending**. The final Agent Host skill/launcher selection passed **251 tests**, the unchanged standalone CLI skill selection passed **3 tests**, and the About-dialog suite passed **12 tests**.
- Complete deterministic runner, Full profile: **1,001 passed, 106 existing pending**. All 10 suite/shard summaries passed: Copilot, Conformance, Claude and Codex each have two shards, plus native Copilot OTel and managed settings. These are shards, not repeated executions. The actual default concurrency was 10 workers.
- Remaining supplemental batch: **118 passed, 7 existing pending**, covering every synthetic-provider entrypoint plus Entra transport and the gated live Codex entrypoint. Together with the separate SDK contracts and prompt matrix, this accounts for all 30 supplemental entrypoints discovered by the inventory.
- Final-revision GitHub workflows passed: [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44160795336), [Component Fixtures](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44160794741), and [CodeQL](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/44160794808).
- Native preflight: all 16 baseline/candidate platform archives match their committed SHA-512 pins; no paths were added or removed across the eight platform packages. Linux x64/arm64 ELF loader and symbol requirements and all 24 Windows x64/arm64 PE import/OS-header inspections are unchanged. All 20 inspected baseline/candidate macOS native signatures verify, with unchanged dylib imports and signing Team ID. The runtime/native macOS deployment floor decreases from 14.0 to 13.0; this is not the entire SDK's minimum because unchanged OneAuth libraries have their own deployment floors.
- A separate native SDK probe, using an isolated synthetic local model and real loopback collector with **default scheduling**, verified actual session-correlated spans, disabled content capture, resource identity, and pre-batch shutdown draining. Observed first export was about 9.9 seconds after turn completion; the second session had no exported span before stop and its spans arrived on stop. This is native SDK evidence, not a packaged Agent Host production-latency claim. Existing packaged routing/warm-policy E2E assertions remain separate.
- **SDK Validation definition 720 passed**, builds `498243` and `498244`, both verified against the exact final revision with default architecture parameters and no SDK/runtime canary overrides. Both overall builds succeeded, all seven desktop architectures compiled, and the actual Agent Host E2E task succeeded on Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS arm64 in both builds. This checkout has no E2E repeat support, so these are two fresh builds rather than checkpointed job retries. Superseded builds `498222`, `498223`, `498224`, `498238`, and `498239` were canceled as revisions changed and are not acceptance evidence.
- **Not run: all four full-app Linux dependency-reference checks** (x64/arm64 × DEB/RPM). Final-source application-artifact downloads encountered repeated TLS resets and timeouts. Replacement streaming transfers were stopped before completion; no application assembly completed and none of these checks ran. The SDK-only native comparisons above passed, but no full-app dependency-reference result is claimed.
- **Targeted RPM reference check passed on x64 and arm64.** Ran the repository's `build/linux/rpm/calculate-deps.ts` helper against the integrity-verified baseline and candidate SDK `runtime.node` and `copilot-runtime` files in a Linux Docker container, applying the full generator's bundled-library exclusions. Both architectures have no added or removed RPM requirements and none absent from `build/linux/rpm/dep-lists.ts`. The SDK upgrade therefore introduces no RPM reference-list additions. This uses actual RPM `find-requires`, not only a symbol-version scan; it does not establish full-app list equality or Debian dependency metadata.
- Download retries: transient registry/API transport failures were retried without product changes. The container's VS Code sysroot downloads timed out; the exact official archives were fetched through the host, verified against the unchanged checked-in SHA-256 pins, and used to warm task-owned helper caches. The repository sysroot helpers then succeeded, but this was preparation, not execution of the full-app checks. Azure ArtifactTool retries failed; replacement authenticated streaming ZIP transfers were stopped before completion. No dependency-reference lists, comparison guards, or integrity checks were weakened.

Pipeline 720 covers Windows x64/arm64, Linux x64/arm64/armhf, macOS x64/arm64 compilation and Windows x64/Linux x64/macOS arm64 Agent Host E2E. macOS E2E uses a separate CI-mode build. It is not a full Product validation: distribution-package generation, signing, Alpine, Web, universal macOS, and full artifact-sanity coverage are excluded.

No new known-issue gates or assertion relaxations are introduced. Existing live-only, credentialed, provider/platform skips and accountable expected failures remain; see `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`. Replay results are not live-model behavioral proof. The actual Azure E2E results are identical across the two fresh builds:

| Platform | Build `498243` | Build `498244` | Execution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows x64 | 967 passed, 140 existing pending | 967 passed, 140 existing pending | Full deterministic selection, all 10 suite/shard summaries passed. |
| Linux x64 | 1,019 passed, 106 existing pending | 1,019 passed, 106 existing pending | 1,001-test full tmpfs selection plus 18 required disk-backed persistence tests; both storage passes succeeded. The disk subset is not counted as another complete execution. |
| macOS arm64 | 1,001 passed, 106 existing pending | 1,001 passed, 106 existing pending | Separate CI-mode build, full deterministic selection, all 10 suite/shard summaries passed. |

The local complete-runner command was `AGENT_HOST_TEST_PROFILE=full pnpm run test-agent-host-e2e` (**passed**, 1,001 tests / 106 existing pending). The four full-app Linux dependency checks were not run; no installer-build, installation, or signing results are claimed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and warm Copilot runtime acquisition, including scoped virtual/credential clients
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CopilotAgent._ensureClient acquires the runtime before session launch. Certificate loading and startup asset resolution precede client.start; independent runtime, ripgrep, telemetry, and optional plugin lookups overlap.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the SDK symlink and check runtime/native/extension assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One realpath followed by five concurrent existence checks per candidate; at most two scope directories and two Linux platform candidates, with early success.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical candidate enumeration and filesystem operations under the @github scope; the diff substitutes @microsoft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asset resolution must finish before the client starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the SDK-owned runtime over spawned stdio.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per acquired client, not per caller or tool. Normal sessions share a client; scoped clients are retained by chat key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: RuntimeConnection.forStdio already spawned the runtime; forSpawnedStdio migrates the configuration without adding another launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: client.start must resolve before callers can launch sessions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct scoped chats requiring clients, versus many ordinary chats sharing one client; bounded platform candidates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal concurrent callers share one startup/retry sequence. Different scoped clients can start independently, as before. The five asset checks within each candidate run concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing _client, _clientStarting, and _ensureClientHealing retain/coalesce normal acquisition. ScopedCopilotClient.starting is shared per chat. Failed starts clear their handles; config-change retries remain bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged host process cardinality and startup ordering from the complete client-options diff and acquisition callers. SDK internal initialization is outside the available implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or inspection of the newly published SDK/native runtime implementation; startup changes internal to that dependency cannot be established from its version number.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable host-side regression: configuration is regrouped while acquisition, reuse, overlap, and cleanup ownership remain unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a chat with plugins, custom agents, MCP servers, BYOK/local models, and optional canvases
Scenarios.CriticalPath: initializeSession prepares customization and sandbox state, then launcher.launch builds configuration, opens one SDK session, lists agents, applies sandbox policy, and optionally configures the execution-subagent tool. Connector reconciliation remains adopted background work rather than a launch prerequisite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve local plugin directories and read authored custom-agent definitions through existing helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing directory validation per supplied local plugin directory and authored-agent reads; ephemeral/virtual paths retain their existing enumeration exclusions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same preparation loops, helpers, gates, and Promise.all; the diff changes where their results are placed in SDK options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration preparation awaits these operations, with independent preparation tasks overlapped by Promise.all.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/resume the session and perform existing agent, sandbox, model-option, and tool-registration RPCs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ordinary open/resume per launch, plus existing conditional finalization RPCs. Existing specific-error fallback/reopen paths remain bounded. Tool definitions are sent as a collection, not one RPC per tool.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same open, agent.list, sandbox apply, conditional descriptors/setTools, verbosity, and tier-reset calls with flat option names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Open and finalization RPCs precede returning the usable wrapper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK-managed MCP initialization and optional connector reconciliation, with configured managed-settings fetching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Effective MCP names combine root servers and explicitly projected plugin overrides; disabled names are deduplicated. Reconciliation is one existing session-level operation, with SDK-internal server traffic not visible here.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same MCP projection, enablement, managed-settings opt-in, and asynchronous connector reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: SDK open-time initialization remains SDK-controlled; connector reconciliation is explicitly not awaited by session opening.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Local plugin directories, authored agents, combined tool definitions, provider/model rows, and distinct enabled MCP server names after overrides and disabled-name deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Preparation tasks overlap. Finalization RPCs retain existing sequential ordering. Independent launches may overlap; no newly introduced per-item process/RPC fan-out was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The runtime client is reused. Execution-subagent availability uses the existing per-session WeakSet after positive discovery. The diff adds only small collection copies of provider/model rows at wrapper construction, not repeated catalog reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that host-side expensive calls, feature gates, and ordering are preserved by the nested option migration; dependency-internal behavior is not inferred.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual filesystem and remote MCP costs depend on configuration and the opaque SDK implementation; no measured durations are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence introduced regression. Rich options are migrated without evidence of additional initialization, higher cardinality, or changed critical-path placement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply live image, permission, sandbox, model, and shell-init configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Live configuration synchronization and turn-start synchronization await existing control-plane RPCs; shell registration first materializes its file and applies the required sandbox grant.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update SDK options using the new inference/tools/experiments/permissions option groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same conditional RPC per changed effective setting. Applied-value checks skip unchanged image/permission state; experimental mode is set only when not already applied; shell registration updates only for a new path or clearing an existing registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same conditions and awaits issued options.update with flat payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required configuration remains awaited before dependent model/tool work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize or rewrite the shell-init script before registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only after the serialized script list differs; changed content can reuse the registered path and avoid another registration RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical serialization check, file helper, path comparison, and sandbox ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First registration requires the file and sandbox configuration before the shell option RPC.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective configuration changes across active sessions, not every notification or every shell command.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing image, permission, and shell sequencers serialize their respective session mutations. The diff changes payload shape, not sequencing or aggregate session concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Applied image flags, permission mode, experimental-mode state, serialized scripts, and registered script path continue suppressing redundant work. Existing inactive-session guards remain.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from changed RPC sites and surrounding applied-state checks/sequencers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: RPC duration and active-session population are unmeasured, but no changed multiplicity or scheduling mechanism is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: expensive boundaries are preserved rather than introduced or moved onto a hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream shell output and attribute live subagent usage
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK shell-output events synchronously dispatch to the existing appendChunk handler and output-terminal manager. Completion/background-shell handling retains its existing ownership and persistence paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive ordered SDK output chunks and forward accepted output through existing terminal channels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing handler per shell_output event; duplicate/out-of-order sequences are rejected by appendChunk. The removed partial-result listener no longer receives obsolete snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shell_output handler and appendChunk implementation already ran; a second snapshot handler was also registered, and append ignored snapshots after chunk mode began.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Accepted chunks update the terminal during the running tool; no new await is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Output bytes and chunk frequency for tracked shell calls, including background commands; subagent usage event frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event callbacks run synchronously on the host event loop. Client-hosted PTY calls remain excluded because their own terminal channel streams output.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing sequence numbers, stream tracking, finalized-state checks, and background-shell ownership remain. Usage attribution now relies on the already-existing envelope-to-subagent mapping rather than legacy duplicate metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that chunk processing was already present and that deleting the snapshot listener introduces neither output fan-out nor a new retention path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK event emission rates are not inspectable; no assumptions are made that the package bump newly enables full-output chunks.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression. Existing transcript accumulation is not attributable to this diff; removal of the obsolete handler alone does not prove a distinct shipped performance-regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore long chat histories, including legacy or damaged journals
Scenarios.CriticalPath: History restoration reads sequential event-log pages, reconstructs turns with stored metadata, and reattaches stored shell-output references before presenting the restored conversation. Recovery streams a fixed journal snapshot when the SDK rejects it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per cursor page; unused event types are filtered as each page arrives.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical pagination and filtering; only the SDK type import changes in this helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All required pages must be read for the complete restored snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read response metadata, batched edit/resource records, and batched terminal-output sizes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing fixed metadata reads plus collection-wide getFileEdits/getToolResultResources calls and one getTerminalOutputSizes call for all shell candidates, not per-event database queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same grouped database reads; changed attribution accesses add only constant-time type/property checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing reads feed reconstruction and output references.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/stat a damaged journal and stream its fixed byte range line by line.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open/stat/stream/close per recovery, with one JSON parse per nonempty record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same fixed snapshot stream and parsing loop; legacy parentToolCallId is now spread from a small temporary object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Recovery must finish before the recovered transcript is returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: History pages, event records, tool calls, and journal bytes; database operations remain grouped over relevant call IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: History pages and journal records are consumed sequentially. Existing batched database lookups remain outside per-event reconstruction loops.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mapping tables are per reconstruction; envelope-to-task lookup remains map-based. No new persistent cache or invalidation policy is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete production mapping/recovery diff and inspected history/database call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Long-session sizes and SDK paging costs vary; no profiling was performed and dependency-level pagination changes cannot be inferred.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable introduced regression: no additional full-history pass, per-event boundary call, or long-lived retention is added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customization catalog policy sessions, Microsoft sign-in, and certificate administration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cold catalog operations acquire a hidden policy session after MCP discovery; Microsoft sign-in creates its authentication session and advances the existing login flow. The certificate CLI starts one empty runtime, performs the requested operation, and stops it in finally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover MCP names, create a hidden no-turn session, and optionally install its current GitHub credential.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery/open sequence for a cold policy session; all discovered server names are disabled together. Warm catalog operations reuse the policy session rather than opening one per catalog item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same discover/create/credential calls, disabled-server deduplication, and disabled heavy features using flat options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold policy-session initialization precedes the requested catalog operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the authentication session, begin/advance login, and disconnect/delete it when released.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session per login attempt or required runtime restoration, not per offered account/model. Login steps remain sequential; ready/restored session reuse is retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same login state machine and cleanup; session options are nested under SDK v2 groups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication must finish before account-dependent work can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start one empty runtime for a certificate command and stop it afterward; the command uses the existing certificate RPC implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime lifecycle per explicit CLI invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical single-client lifecycle using forStdio and flat process/auth options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Start, requested certificate operation, and shutdown are awaited for the command result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Catalog requests sharing a live policy session, explicit login attempts, and explicit certificate commands; not catalog entries or account choices.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent policy users share one creation promise. Microsoft restoration is sequenced; login advances await each step. Certificate execution is a single explicit operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Policy-session creation is coalesced with policySessionCreation, reused for the same client, and released after the existing ten-minute idle timeout or replacement. Microsoft session restoration remains sequenced and reuses the active authentication session. Token-provider refresh remains coalesced by _pendingRefresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged session/process counts, disabled-feature options, and cleanup from callers and lifecycle owners.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network authentication and SDK-side managed-policy costs are not measured or independently inspectable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: hidden-session laziness, warm reuse, credential refresh coalescing, and cleanup remain intact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build/package desktop and remote products, including canary and universal/snap builds
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Build-time SDK version resolution and target-platform package availability precede product packaging; canary registry resolution precedes lockfile refresh. These are build paths, not editor interaction paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the package registry through existing pnpm view commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime-version query for an explicit canary version; the latest-canary sentinel adds the existing versions query. No per-runtime-platform registry query is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queries remain synchronous prerequisites within the opt-in canary build.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize a missing target package with existing npm pack, integrity verification, and extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected target package per install root when missing; an existing package returns immediately, and a matching pnpm virtual-store copy is linked without packing. Existing retry cap is three transient pack attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same availability checks, cache paths, retry behavior, and extraction for the old package scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before packaging the target payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read SDK metadata, copy selected native payloads, and apply existing archive/universal/snap processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same selected-target include/exclude structure; universal builds still combine two architectures. Optional heavyweight native payload exclusions remain unchanged apart from scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same payload selection and processing with @github/copilot-sdk paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Build targets, the desktop/remote install roots, and payload bytes; no newly expanded architecture set or per-file subprocess loop is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Registry/materialization subprocesses remain synchronous within their build step; pipeline and packaging concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing package and pnpm virtual-store hits avoid downloading; missing packages follow the existing bounded materialization path. The dependency is replaced, not added alongside the old SDK in the importer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged host boundary cardinality and artifact filtering from build diffs and ensureNpmPackage.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Published tarball sizes and native SDK implementation costs are unavailable; version changes alone do not prove a size or build-time regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No concrete introduced performance regression identified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display Copilot versions in the native About dialog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Format the existing product-version metadata into the dialog details string.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed number of version strings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Constant-size synchronous string formatting as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses already-present product metadata; no new lookup or cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines only rename the SDK dependency key and displayed label.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material performance magnitude uncertainty for the shown constant-size change.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass for PR #348894 using the host-supplied comparison. Inspected the complete paginated 161-file inventory and relevant production diff pages, plus supporting tests and transitive lifecycle/boundary code. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance finding or concrete regression-fix provenance qualified for submission. Main limitation: published SDK/native runtime implementation and measured performance were not available, so dependency-internal behavior was not inferred from the version bump.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
